summary: Out-of-band embedding metadata header causing rerank mismatches and request-side backpressure
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a regression where rerank results intermittently return no hits or dramatically different top-k ordering and the request pipeline experiences increased latencies and client-side backpressure. Root cause appears linked to an out-of-band HTTP header (custom proxy) that appends embedding metadata which the embedding ingestion path is incorrectly interpreting as a separate embedding bundle, causing dimension/namespace mismatches and downstream queueing.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests from Acme Health see rerank topk inversion and occasional 504s due to long queue wait times.
- Affects enterprise traffic routed through an ingestion proxy in us-east.
- Customer workflows that depend on stable rerank ordering for clinical search are impacted.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (k8s autoscale pool #7)
- API gateway: redwood-edge-v2 behind customer proxy
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends embed+rerank batch via their proxy which attaches header 'X-Embed-Meta: namespace=clinical|version=202602' and a JSON blob in an out-of-band header.
2) Requests enter Redwood API gateway, are routed to embedding-service for ingest, then to reranker for scoring.
3) Observe intermittent rerank empty results, top-k reorder, and elevated p95/p99 latency on the request path.
4) Reproduced locally by simulating header injection and sending mixed-batch embeddings (compact and float32) in a single call.
Expected: Rerank should honor the client's explicit namespace/version without causing embedding shape or route confusion; latency should remain within SLOs.

investigation_notes: 03/12 11:00 — Triage: Customer CS provided logs and cURL reproducer that includes 'X-Embed-Meta' header. Initial suspicion: header parsing collision in embed ingest path.

03/12 12:30 — SRE attached heap/queue metrics (link: https://prometheus.redwood/internal/d/ingest/queue?var-cluster=prod-us-east) showing spikes in embed-ingest queue and rerank queue concurrent with customer traffic bursts.

03/12 13:45 — Reproduced locally by injecting header; observed ingest-service creating a logical second entry for namespace=clinical, which triggered a model-selection mismatch (compact vs float32 dims). This forced reranker to call CPU fallback path causing latency and queueing.

Hypothesis: The ingest proxy is using an out-of-band header carrying a serialized embedding meta object. Our ingest path attempted to accept the header as an alternate embedding payload when bodies are mixed (binary + header), leading to dimension mapping errors.

Temporary mitigation tested: Ignore 'X-Embed-Meta' if content-length of header > 256 bytes OR when body indicates a separate embedding bundle. This reduced queue growth in canary by ~80% in 30 minutes.
Related artifacts: Slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02SUP) and GH repro (https://github.com/redwood-inference/issue-repros/pull/56).

resolution_notes: 03/13 02:00 — Mitigation: Rolled out ingest-gateway config to ignore X-Embed-Meta header if header payload length > 128 or header contains JSON-like blob; this prevented treating header as embedded payload.
03/13 04:30 — Prod rollback: Customer rolled back proxy header injection for their traffic window as a coordinated safety measure.
03/14 09:00 — Hotfix PR merged (ingest-gateway #412): explicit header whitelist and schema validation for embedding payloads. Auto-reject with clear 400 and log when unsupported header detected.
